cvEn:
Tova-Mira Taub, daughter of Tzvi and Sara, was born on the 15th of Adar I 5711 (21 February 1951) in Beersheba. She received her primary education at the "Degania" school and her secondary education at the Beersheba Comprehensive High School A. She enlisted in the IDF in mid-October 1969 and was assigned to the Armored Corps.

She always strove to bring a homely warmth into the army camp. She decorated every place she was in with flowers, plants, pictures and maps, to make her surroundings more pleasant and cheerful. She was a lively, joyful girl, and for that reason she was the center of the social circle. She always tried to encourage her friends to lift their spirits, even in difficult hours, and to share with them the joy of life she carried within her.

She worked as a draftswoman and fulfilled her role properly, but she hoped to transfer to a unit in which women and men serve together. Her joy knew no bounds when she was finally transferred to a battalion. She was kind-hearted and devoted to her duties. Even when additional tasks were assigned to her, such as work at the switchboard, she did not accept them with reluctance, as other girls did, but carried out whatever was required of her willingly. When the forces went out on an exercise or an operation, she would ask to join them.

She was deeply devoted to her home and family, and she never forgot to call home to send her greetings of peace, even when the hour was late or when her work was heavy. On the 7th of Iyar 5731 (2 May 1971), she lost her life while carrying out her duties. She was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Beersheba.

Her commander wrote to her family in a letter of condolence: "Through her conduct, her character and her joy of life, Tova won the hearts of the soldiers of the unit and its commanders. Throughout her entire service she carried out every task assigned to her in the best possible way, and all of this with a smile on her lips. As someone who worked with Tova in daily contact, I came to know her qualities and her character closely, and I was proud that such soldiers served in my unit. Her memory will remain with us."

The first pages of the booklet "Apikim BaNegev," the journal of the Beersheba Comprehensive High School A, in the section "Yad LeNof'lim" (A Memorial for the Fallen), are dedicated to her memory.
